verdict.rationale: Cline's own Kanban feature documents auto-commit and isolated per-card git worktrees, which covers the agent committing changes and working on separate branches-like workspaces. Nothing in the evidence shows the agent writing commit messages, explicitly creating named branches, or opening pull requests. Generic terminal-command execution is not credited as a git workflow feature. missing for 10: documented commit-message generation, explicit branch creation, pull request creation, explicit staging control outside Kanban, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent stage changes, write commit messages, create branches, and open pull requests

citations.quote: Run many agents in parallel from a web-based task board with per-card worktrees, auto-commit, and dependency chains.
Use Cline Kanban to run multiple coding agents in parallel with isolated git worktrees.
